51.solution:
A salt that turns blue litmus red gives an acidic solution.
\(\text{CuCl}_2\) is the salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base \(\text{Cu(OH)}_2\), so it hydrolyses to give an acidic solution.
KCN and \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) are salts of weak acids and strong bases (basic); \(\text{NaNO}_3\) is neutral.

52.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
52.solution:
Wurtz reaction of \(\text{CH}_3\text{Br}\) and \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}\) with Na/dry ether gives all cross- and self-coupling products:
\(\text{CH}_3\)–\(\text{CH}_3\) (ethane), \(\text{CH}_3\)–\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) (propane) and \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\)–\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) (butane).
Pentane (5 C) cannot form from a C1 + C2 coupling, so it is NOT obtained.

53.solution:
A reducing agent gets oxidised (loses electrons). The weakest reducing agent is the species least able to lose electrons.
\(F^-\) already holds an extra electron tightly (F is the most electronegative element), so it has essentially no tendency to be oxidised further — it is the weakest reducing agent.
Li loses an electron readily (strong reductant); \(F_2\) is a strong oxidant; \(\text{Li}^+\) cannot reduce easily but \(F^-\) is the standard textbook answer for weakest reducing agent.

54.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
54.solution:
The structure is an open-chain ether: \(\text{CH}_3\)–O–\(\text{CH}_2\)–C(\(\text{CH}_3\))\(_2\)–\(\text{CH}_2\)–\(\text{CH}_3\).
Parent chain = butane; the methoxy group is on C1 and two methyl groups on C2.
Name: 1-Methoxy-2,2-dimethylbutane. The skeleton is acyclic, ruling out the cyclobutane options.

55.solution:
\(\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ\), taking \(T = 298\,\text{K}\).
\(\Delta H^\circ = \Delta G^\circ + T\Delta S^\circ = 28000 + 298 \times 120 = 28000 + 35760 = 63760\,\text{J}\).
\(\Delta H^\circ = 63.76\,\text{kJ}\).

56.solution:
Mass of unit cell \(= \rho \times a^3 = 3.2 \times 10^{-22}\,\text{g}\).
Number of particles \(n = \dfrac{\text{mass of unit cell}}{\text{mass of one particle}} = \dfrac{3.2 \times 10^{-22}}{8.0 \times 10^{-23}} = 4\).

57.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
57.solution:
Coupling of benzene diazonium chloride with phenol (an azo coupling) is carried out in mild alkaline medium.
The base converts phenol to the more reactive phenoxide ion, which couples at the para position to give p-hydroxyazobenzene.

58.solution:
Eugenol is the principal aromatic constituent obtained from clove oil.
(Wintergreen gives methyl salicylate; Indian gooseberry/citrus give vitamin C-type acids.)

59.solution:
Adsorption is exothermic, so the extent of adsorption (x/m) is highest at the lowest temperature.
From the isobars, the 195 K curve lies highest, so the greatest amount of gas is adsorbed at 195 K.

60.solution:
Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, forms only one oxoacid, HOF (hypofluorous acid), in which O is the central atom and F shows oxidation state \(-1\).
Higher oxoacids \(\text{HFO}_2\), \(\text{HFO}_3\), \(\text{HFO}_4\) do not exist because F cannot expand its valence/show positive oxidation states.

61.solution:
Ethers are basic at the oxygen atom (lone pairs). With cold concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) they dissolve by accepting a proton on oxygen to form an oxonium (dialkyl oxonium) salt.
\(\text{R}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow [\text{R}_2\text{OH}]^+ \text{HSO}_4^-\).

62.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
62.solution:
\(W = -P_{ext}\Delta V = -P_{ext}(V_2 - V_1)\).
\(W = -4\,\text{bar} \times (13 - 25)\,\text{dm}^3 = -4 \times (-12) = 48\,\text{dm}^3\,\text{bar}\).
Using \(1\,\text{dm}^3\,\text{bar} = 100\,\text{J}\): \(W = 48 \times 100 = 4800\,\text{J}\) (work done on the gas).

64.solution:
Myosin is a fibrous protein (muscle protein), whereas legumelin, egg albumin and insulin are globular proteins.
Hence myosin is NOT a globular protein.

65.subtopic: Industrial Processes, Minerals, Hydrogen Compounds and Alloys
65.solution: Bronze is an alloy of copper (Cu) and tin (Sn); it is tough, strong and corrosion resistant and is used for making statues, medals and trophies.

66.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
66.solution:
% atom economy \(= \dfrac{\text{formula mass of desired product}}{\text{sum of formula masses of all reactants}} \times 100\).
Reactants: chloroethane 64.5 g + KOH 56 g = 120.5 g; product ethanol = 46 g.
\(= \dfrac{46}{120.5} \times 100 = 38.17\%\).

68.subtopic: Group 16 Chalcogens, Oxygen, Sulphur and Ozone
68.solution:
Ozone is a strong OXIDISING agent (not reducing), has an angular (bent) shape, acts as a bleaching agent and absorbs harmful UV radiation.
Hence the incorrect statement is that it is a strong reducing agent.

69.solution: Kolbe's reaction: sodium phenoxide + \(\text{CO}_2\) at 398 K / 6 atm gives sodium salicylate (A); acidification with \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^+\) gives salicylic acid (B).

70.subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model, de Broglie, Heisenberg and Quantum Numbers
70.solution:
Four of the five d-orbitals (\(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{xz}, d_{x^2-y^2}\)) have a four-lobed (clover-leaf) shape.
\(d_{z^2}\) has a different shape — two lobes along the z-axis plus a doughnut-shaped ring in the xy-plane.

71.solution:
Equal osmotic pressure (isotonic) needs equal molar concentration: \(\dfrac{W}{M}\) equal for both.
Urea: \(\dfrac{3}{60} = 0.05\,\text{mol}\); Sucrose: \(\dfrac{17.1}{342} = 0.05\,\text{mol}\).
Thus 3 g/L urea and 17.1 g/L sucrose are isotonic.

72.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
72.solution: Maltose is formed from two \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units joined by a glycosidic bond between C-1 of one and C-4 of the other, i.e. an \(\alpha\)-1,4 glycosidic linkage.

73.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
73.solution: Among the given lanthanoids, ytterbium (Yb, [Xe]\(4f^{14}6s^2\)) has the highest first ionisation enthalpy because of the extra stability of its completely filled \(4f^{14}\) subshell.

74.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
74.solution:
The unit of the rate constant is \((\text{time})^{-1}\) (here hour\(^{-1}\)), which is the unit for a first-order rate constant.
Hence the order of reaction is 1.

76.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
76.solution:
The molecule is \(F_2\) (18 electrons). MO configuration:
\((\sigma 1s)^2(\sigma^*1s)^2(\sigma 2s)^2(\sigma^*2s)^2(\sigma 2p_z)^2(\pi 2p_x)^2(\pi 2p_y)^2(\pi^*2p_x)^2(\pi^*2p_y)^2\).
Bonding electrons = 10, antibonding electrons = 8.

77.solution:
An \(S_N1\) reaction proceeds via a planar carbocation, so racemization occurs only when the carbon bearing the leaving group is a chiral (stereo) centre.
(A) 2-chloropropane and (C) 3-chloropentane have no stereocentre (two identical groups on the C–Cl carbon); (D) neopentyl chloride is primary and achiral.
(B) 2-chlorobutane has a chiral carbon (Cl, H, \(\text{CH}_3\), \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\)), so it racemizes via \(S_N1\).

78.solution: Reduction of the carbonyl group (>C=O) to methylene (>CH\(_2\)) using hydrazine followed by heating with NaOH/KOH in ethylene glycol is the Wolff-Kishner reduction.

80.solution:
Nylon 6,6 is a polyamide, having repeating amide \(-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-\) inter-unit linkages.
SBR is a copolymer rubber, melamine-formaldehyde and bakelite are cross-linked resins.

81.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
81.solution:
In \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\), Co is +3: \(3d^6\).
\(\text{NH}_3\) is a strong-field ligand, so the complex is low-spin (\(d^2sp^3\)): all six d-electrons pair in \(t_{2g}\) (\(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\)).
Number of unpaired electrons = zero.

83.solution:
In Merck's process, hydrogen peroxide is prepared by treating sodium peroxide \(\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2\) with dilute (cold) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\):
\(\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2\).

84.solution:
The products 2-chloroacetophenone and 4-chloroacetophenone are ortho/para acetylation products of a chloro-substituted benzene.
Friedel-Crafts acylation of chlorobenzene with acetyl chloride/anhydrous \(\text{AlCl}_3\) gives exactly these o- and p-chloroacetophenones (Cl is an o,p-director).
Hence A = chlorobenzene.

85.solution:

Moles \(= \dfrac{8}{32} = 0.25\,\text{mol}\).
Volume at STP \(= 0.25 \times 22.4 = 5.6\,\text{dm}^3\).

87.solution:
Adipic acid is \(\text{HOOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{COOH}\), a 6-carbon dicarboxylic acid with both COOH groups at chain ends.
Oxidative cleavage of cyclohexene (ring C=C) with hot acidic \(\text{KMnO}_4\) opens the ring to give a single straight-chain product, adipic acid.
The acyclic hexenes would give two separate fragments, not adipic acid.

88.solution: \(\Delta T_b = K_b \cdot m\) so \(m = \dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b} = \dfrac{0.39}{0.52} = 0.75\,\text{mol kg}^{-1}\).

89.solution: Buna-N (nitrile rubber, a copolymer of buta-1,3-diene and acrylonitrile) is oil- and heat-resistant and is used to make conveyor/rubber belts, hoses and gaskets.

90.solution:
Isothiocyanato (\(\text{NCS}^-\)) carries a negative charge and is an anionic ligand.
Ammine (\(\text{NH}_3\)), aqua (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) and ethylenediamine are neutral ligands.

92.solution:
Calcium phosphate is \(\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2\). Let oxidation number of P be x.
\(3(+2) + 2x + 8(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow 6 + 2x - 16 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5\).

93.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
93.solution:
Dehydration of an alcohol with conc. \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) gives an alkene; 2-methylbutan-1-ol dehydrates via a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable 3\(^\circ\) carbocation, giving 2-methylbut-2-ene (Saytzeff product).
Thus the compound forming 2-methylbut-2-ene is the alcohol 2-methylbutan-1-ol; option A names the alkene product 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is the keyed answer per the reproduced paper.
93.note: Option set as reproduced is internally odd (the stem asks which compound 'forms' 2-methylbut-2-ene, yet option A is 2-methylbut-2-ene itself). The keyed answer A is preserved as printed; among the alcohols offered, dehydration giving 2-methylbut-2-ene corresponds to 2-methylbutan-1-ol via hydride shift.

95.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
95.solution:
Malonic, glutaric and succinic acids are dicarboxylic acids.
Caproic acid, \(\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}\), is a monocarboxylic acid (hexanoic acid), so it is NOT a dicarboxylic acid.

96.subtopic: Enthalpy and Relation Between ΔH and ΔU
96.solution:
Endothermic processes absorb heat. Melting of ice, \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(s)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)}\), absorbs heat (\(\Delta_{fus}H = +6.01\,\text{kJ/mol}\)).
Freezing and condensation (the other options) are exothermic.

97.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
97.solution:
A p-type semiconductor is made by doping silicon (group 14) with a group-13 element (3 valence electrons), which creates holes.
Gallium (Ga) is the group-13 dopant; Sb, As and P are group-15 (give n-type).

98.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
98.solution:
Lowest \(pK_b\) means strongest base. Ethylamine \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2\) (\(pK_b \approx 3.29\)) is the strongest base of the set due to the +I effect of the alkyl group and good solvation of its ammonium ion.
Aromatic amines (aniline) are much weaker; trimethylamine and benzylamine have higher \(pK_b\).

99.solution:
Furan, THF (tetrahydrofuran) and 4H-pyran are oxygen heterocycles.
Pyrrole contains nitrogen as the heteroatom (not oxygen), so it does NOT contain oxygen as a heteroatom.

100.solution:
Moles of \(\text{CH}_4 = \dfrac{1.6}{16} = 0.1\,\text{mol}\); molecules \(= 0.1 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 6.022 \times 10^{22}\).
Each \(\text{CH}_4\) has 10 electrons (6 from C + 4 from H).
Total electrons \(= 6.022 \times 10^{22} \times 10 = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\).
